quickSummary: Cell cycle transitions are driven by Cyclins (regulatory subunits whose concentrations oscillate) and Cyclin-Dependent Kinases (CDKs, catalytic serine/threonine kinases). G1 progression relies on Cyclin D-CDK4/6. G1/S transition requires Cyclin E-CDK2. S-phase replication is driven by Cyclin A-CDK2. Entry into M-phase is propelled by the MPF complex (Cyclin B-CDK1).

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Cyclins are regulatory subunits; CDKs are catalytic kinases. Cyclin B + CDK1 forms MPF (Maturation-Promoting Factor).

     ┌───────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┐

  G₁/S CHECKPOINT                 G₂/M CHECKPOINT            SPINDLE ASSEMBLY CHECKPOINT

conceptBreakdown.content:
Transitions through cell cycle phases are strictly regulated by protein complexes formed by:
• **Cyclins**: Regulatory proteins whose intracellular levels oscillate systematically throughout the cycle.
• **Cyclin-Dependent Kinases (CDKs)**: Serine/threonine protein kinases that remain at relatively constant levels but are catalytically active only when bound to their cognate cyclin partner.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 2.1 Phase-Specific Cyclin-CDK Matrix
conceptBreakdown.title: 2.1 Phase-Specific Cyclin-CDK Matrix
conceptBreakdown.content:
| Cell Cycle Transition | Regulatory Cyclin Subunit | Catalytic CDK Partner | Key Downstream Substrates |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **$G_1$ Phase Progression** | **Cyclin D** (D1, D2, D3) | **CDK4 / CDK6** | Retinoblastoma Protein ($\text{Rb}$) phosphorylation |
| **$G_1/S$ Transition** | **Cyclin E** | **CDK2** | $\text{E2F}$ transcription factor liberation; centrosome duplication |
| **$S$ Phase Progression** | **Cyclin A** | **CDK2** | DNA pre-replication complex activation (MCM helicase) |
| **$G_2/M$ Transition** | **Cyclin B** | **CDK1 (CDC2)** | **MPF Complex**; Lamin phosphorylation (nuclear envelope breakdown) |
